props.covers: Baseline preparation, staged reconciliation, and confirmed atomic publication for sync.

text.insert: This page carries the detailed preparation, reconciliation, and publication contract behind the
Sync Workflow
Baseline Preparation
The preparation boundary establishes one comparison point for reconciliation:
Fetch the configured remote and verify the observed upstream head.
Refresh the game upstream worktree without mutating the control checkout.
Confirm that the cycle tree is clean at its recorded
head_revision
Discover merged-PR intake, open-PR reconciliation needs, and staged knowledge sources.
Record the requested baseline, worktree identities, intake set, and trace lineage.

Repeated preparation reuses clean cycle state only when its ancestry is compatible with the requested baseline. Ambiguous ancestry, dirty protected worktrees, or stale observations block activation instead of being repaired implicitly.
Staged Reconciliation
Sync performs all pre-publication work in an isolated staging worktree. The cycle tree and
head_revision
remain byte-identical until publication.
The staged workflow:
Ingest merged-PR evidence and sync-classified knowledge sources.
Reconcile cycle history against the requested upstream baseline.
Reconcile open PR series against the staged history.
Route bounded mechanical conflicts automatically and minor semantic conflicts to agents.
Preserve staging and block when a conflict cannot be resolved confidently.
Build and validate the complete staged result.
Cancellation before publication discards staging without compensation. Crash recovery resumes a durable stage or discards it at the operator's direction.
Knowledge jobs retain their own lifecycle and provenance.
Execution Classes and Jobs
defines background-safe work, sync-stage work, and publication behavior.
Why Sync Stages Before Anchoring
Staging makes publication the first point at which the active cycle can change. Sync rests at
validated

after reconciliation and validation, so the operator may confirm publish or cancel. Confirmed source publication repoints the clean cycle to the validated staging head before durable lineage commits, while a pre-durability failure compensates back to the prior head.
The complete staged-reconciliation-to-publication sequence keeps the mutation boundary explicit:

steps.text: prepare and record the baseline comparison point
ingest merged-PR evidence and sync-classified knowledge into staging
reconcile cycle history against the requested upstream baseline
reconcile open PR series against staged history
route bounded conflicts and block on conflicts that cannot be resolved confidently
build and validate the staged result to reach validated
recheck upstream and the clean cycle tree, then repoint to the staged head
complete PR-branch pushes, mark published, release the lease, and pin boundary evidence

text.insert: Confirmed Publication

props.title: Decision (2026-08-12) — sync reconciles in staging and publishes atomically

text.insert: Sync reconciles in an isolated staging worktree and leaves the cycle untouched until the operator confirms publication. A source-changing publish performs the non-fast-forward cycle repoint, transactionally records the remote_application entry, invalidations, and monotonic knowledge revision, completes reconciled PR-branch pushes while publishing, and captures a boundary save-point anchor at the published head.
validated
is the stable operator gate between preparation and mutation. Only confirmed
sync.publish
enters the non-cancellable publication path.
Publication:
Rechecks that upstream matches the validated target and the cycle tree is clean at the recorded prior head.
Repoints the cycle tree to the validated staging head, including a validated non-fast-forward move when required.
Atomically records the cycle head, upstream anchor,
remote_application
, invalidations, PR-push intents, and monotonic knowledge revision.
Completes reconciled PR-branch pushes under lease protection.
Marks sync published, releases dispatch authority, and pins boundary evidence to the published head.
A knowledge-only publication advances the monotonic knowledge revision without moving the cycle head, recording
remote_application
, creating source invalidations, or pushing PR branches. Transaction or push failure leaves sync blocked with durable recovery state; it never degrades to a log-only warning.
Publication concludes with
boundary save-point capture
, while the
event-level contract
defines the durable sync and knowledge events emitted across the boundary.
